title: Mao's 1927 Hunan report is his investigation of the peasant movement, in his own categories
summary: Mao's March 1927 Hunan report is his own political account of the peasant movement.
body: Fordham prints Mao's March 1927 report on the peasant movement in Hunan. The report is Mao's political investigation and his judgment of the movement. It is not a census of Hunan and not a rival party's report. The wording on the page includes: "firmly oppose it. Source: Mao Zedong [Mao Tse-tung]: Report on an Investigation of the Peasant Movement in Hunan, March 1927, in Selected Works of Mao Tse-tung, vol. I (3rd printing; Peking: Foreign Languages Press, 1975), pp. 23-29 This text is part of the Internet Modern History Sourcebook. The Sourcebook is a collection of public domain and copy-permitted texts for". The evidence label is the truth-gate ceiling for this host. The host is not on the gate's primary-text or official list, so the label is weak. The quotation is still the page's wording.
